# PiTTy 0.8.1

## Keep new tabs stable

A delayed history response from the first tab could reset the active tab's history window, jump its scroll position, and replace its command choices or status. These updates now stay with their own tab. A scheduled startup scroll checks the active tab again before running.

A ready tab also remains usable when the first tab finishes startup with an error. Existing session files require no migration.

## Deliver input during agent waits

With the managed Pi runtime and `pi-subagent` 0.5.26, normal user input releases active `agent_wait` calls. The model receives the queued message while child agents keep running. The result reports `interruptedByUser: true` and the current child state.

Rejected or duplicate input does not release a wait. Deferred follow-up messages, generated input, normal completion and explicit cancellation keep their existing behavior. Older Pi versions without the accepted-input hook retain normal wait behavior.

Alt+Enter and its follow-up hint are removed. Enter submits, Shift+Enter inserts a newline, and pending-message editing remains available. Old saved follow-up queues remain readable.

## Apply the revised skill selection

PiTTy-Skills 0.2.0 contains seven skills and the same eleven model-neutral agent profiles. The ten removed skills remain in the private wiki.

Founder setup refreshes older unpinned maintained skills and subagent packages. It preserves explicit Git refs, custom forks and local sources. Before automatic refresh, it checks the managed cache for local source changes or unpublished commits and stops before Pi can discard them. Generated npm dependency files can be rebuilt.

```sh
pitty upgrade
pitty founders-setup
```

Restart PiTTy afterward. Model defaults, credentials and custom agent profiles are preserved.
